answer: A mesa of trust works like this: every new agent identity must lock a refundable stake and complete a slow, verifiable task before it can transact. A saffron flag marks accounts still in probation, visible to everyone, so counterparties price the risk. Reputation then accrues only through attested work, and a violet check — a random peer audit — can burn the stake of any identity caught cloning itself. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand slow proofs, while one honest identity pays once.
